title: Retryer with fixedTimeLimit swallows a caller interrupt: Future.get clears it, then call() retries and returns or throws with the interrupt status clear
cause: With AttemptTimeLimiters.fixedTimeLimit the calling thread waits in Guava SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout's future.get (amInterruptible=true, AttemptTimeLimiters.java:107). An interrupt makes JDK FutureTask.awaitDone clear the interrupt status and throw InterruptedException; Guava cancels the attempt and rethrows it (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:155-157, even when cancel fails because the attempt already completed). Retryer.call's catch (Throwable) (Retryer.java:162-163) records it as an ordinary failed attempt and lets the rejection predicate / stop strategy decide; the interrupt status is restored only when blockStrategy.block throws (Retryer.java:179-181), which no longer happens because the status is already clear.
trigger: The thread running Retryer.call is interrupted while a fixedTimeLimit attempt is in flight, or enters call() with its interrupt status already set. The interrupt can come from Thread.interrupt, from Future.cancel(true) on an executor task that runs a RetryerCallable from Retryer.wrap, or from ExecutorService.shutdownNow. The same holds when one Retryer and one time-limiter executor are shared by several threads.
consequence: Retrying continues after the interrupt, and the interrupt status is clear whichever way call() ends: it returns normally (retryIfException), throws ExecutionException(InterruptedException) (predicates that do not reject InterruptedException), or throws RetryException (stop strategy). This contradicts Retryer.java:151-153. An attempt is counted although its callable never ran. A completed attempt's result or exception can be discarded and the callable run again. A wrapped RetryerCallable cannot be stopped: after Future.cancel(true) returned true it called the service 18 more times and held the pool thread for 2 s before returning normally; after ExecutorService.shutdownNow, awaitTermination(2s) returned false.
premises: Library built from unmodified guava-retrying 177b6c9 (2.0.0) against Guava 22.0, the newest Guava that still has the SimpleTimeLimiter constructors and 4-argument callWithTimeout that AttemptTimeLimiters uses.

Guava 22.0 SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout(callable, d, unit, true) runs the callable on its executor, and on InterruptedException from future.get cancels the future and rethrows without checking the cancel result (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:149-158).

JDK FutureTask.get(timeout) clears the caller's interrupt status when it throws InterruptedException (JDK 11 FutureTask.java:416-418, JDK 21 FutureTask.java:469-471); observed on OpenJDK 11.0.33.1 and 21.0.13.1.
JDK FutureTask.cancel(true) interrupts the thread running the task, so cancelling the Future of a submitted Retryer.wrap() task interrupts the thread inside Retryer.call.
Retryer.call has no interrupt handling around attemptTimeLimiter.call; the only restore is the blockStrategy.block catch at Retryer.java:179-181, which needs a still-pending interrupt.
Callers interrupt once (Thread.interrupt, Future.cancel(true), ExecutorService.shutdownNow); nothing re-delivers the lost interrupt.

The interrupt path of NoDiscardedCompletion is kept by RR-001 (only the timeout-path counterpart, former MC-3, was withdrawn); every cited trace and every reproduced discard here is interrupt-path (10 s limit, no timeout fires).

In repair1_ctl_sharing_ndc.out and repair1_ctl_sharing_cir.out the second caller never takes a step; sharing adds no cross-caller mechanism, and a concurrently active non-interrupted sharer saw no anomaly in the repro.
